title: DexArena — Long-Horizon Dexterous Manipulation
text: Open drawer Open laptop Insert rail Long-horizon dexterous manipulation DexArena Dexterity over long horizons. Execute precise skills, generalize across scenes, and compose behavior into complete bimanual tasks. Discover the research ↗ Cross-scene evaluation · 90 combinations Same skill. New scene. Change the scene. Keep the task. Evaluate all 30 canonical stages on three native scene surfaces with fixed policy cameras. Explore generalization ↗ Featured task · Bimanual dexterity Two hands. One task. Open the package. Retrieve the apple. Coordinate both hands to open the flaps, then grasp and place the apple: two connected stages with physical success conditions. title: Tasks — DexArena
text: Simulation benchmark Task catalog 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level environments, all verified against the current SoftHandGrasping codebase. 10 sequences 30 stages All Household Industrial Laboratory Office Search 01 Household · 3 stages Meal Preparation Open a lunch box, place bread on a plate, then use a spoon to scoop and transfer a tomato. Explore task ↗ 02 Household · 4 stages Cabinet & Pouring Open a cabinet, retrieve and place a bottle, unscrew and place its cap, then pour the contents into a bowl. Explore task ↗ 03 Household · 3 stages Drawer & Plug Open the middle drawer, retrieve a charger, place it on the table, and align both prongs into a socket. Explore task ↗ 04 Industrial · 3 stages Nut & Bolt Stand a bolt upright, seat a nut on its axis, then rotate the nut counterclockwise through a full half turn. Explore task ↗ 05 Office · 3 stages Office Desk Open a laptop, type PAIR followed by Enter, and complete the sequence with a left mouse click. Explore task ↗ 06 Industrial · 3 stages Furniture Assembly Lay a panel flat, slide a rail into its groove, and fasten it by turning a wing screw by hand. Explore task ↗ 07 Laboratory · 2 stages Pipette Transfer Aspirate from a sample cup, return the pipette, then dispense into a target well and return it again. Explore task ↗ 08 Household · 5 stages Juice Preparation Open a refrigerator, move an apple into a blender, close the door, place the lid, and press the power button. Explore task ↗ 09 Household · 2 stages Package Opening Open both package flaps with two hands, then extract the apple and place it stably on the plate. Explore task ↗ 10 Household · 2 stages Table Cleaning Pick three debris blocks into a dustpan, then tip all three into a trash bin. Explore task ↗

Understand what is measured before comparing scores. Open a topic for track definitions, metric details or reproducibility requirements. 01 Evaluation tracks & native scenes 30 stages, three kitchens and ten complete sequences DexArena separates failures in execution, generalization and composition while preserving matching task definitions. 01 · Stage level Skill execution Run each of the 30 canonical stage environments with its registered robot, horizon, action layout and physical success predicate. 50 evaluation episodes per stage in the training scene Each stage starts from its own valid reset distribution Persistent success, not transient contact 29-D single-arm or 58-D bimanual Sharpa actions 02 · Scene level Visual generalization Evaluate every stage on three native scene surfaces using identical object placement and the fixed 256 × 256 policy camera rig. 30 stages × 3 native scenes × 50 episodes 90 task × scene combinations Freeze the policy; no further adaptation Retain the background manifest for every run 03 · Sequence level Skill composition Execute two to five dependent stages in their parent long-horizon environment and report complete-sequence success. 10 sequences × 50 episodes Stage progress and terminal success Reset once per episode; inherited state between stages Single-arm and bimanual tasks The canonical data and reported scores use Panda arms with Sharpa hands. Absolute joint-position targets use pd_joint_pos : 7 arm + 22 hand targets for a single arm; left arm 7 → right arm 7 → left hand 22 → right hand 22 for bimanual control. Simulation also supports parallel-jaw grippers, Wuji and XHand, with embodiment-specific action spaces; that support does not imply a scored result matrix for each end-effector. One task. Three native scenes. The same pipette workstation in blue stone, light wood and warm wood kitchens. All 30 stages are evaluated across these three native backgrounds with fixed policy cameras and shared task definitions. Blue kitchen Stone island robocasa_l3_s2 Light wood kitchen Wood island robocasa_l3_s1 Warm wood kitchen Stone island robocasa_l3_s6 An optional LabUtopia laboratory is available for further studies; it is not part of the three native-scene leaderboard matrix. 02 Metrics & aggregation Success predicates, equal task weights and scene-level uncertainty Report the failure mode, not only the final number. Keep task horizons and physical success predicates fixed; persistent hold counters and latches are part of the task definition. Stage Success Rate Fraction of evaluation episodes whose stage predicate is satisfied for its required hold duration. Cross-scene Average Mean stage success over robocasa_l3_s2 , robocasa_l3_s1 and robocasa_l3_s6 . Record the episode-seed manifest used for every scene. Generalization Gap Difference between the reference collection workspace and native-scene performance. Composition Rate Fraction of complete long-horizon episodes reaching the final task success state. Equal task weights. Scene-level uncertainty. Stage and long-horizon averages weight tasks equally. For cross-scene results, average stage success within each scene first, then report the mean and standard deviation across the three scene averages. The ± value is scene variation, not a training-seed confidence interval. 03 Episode protocol & stage transitions Evaluation seeds, frozen policies and transitions without resets All six baselines use image observations and robot proprioception, with matched task horizons, randomization and embodiments. Stage and long-horizon success are measured over 50 episodes per task; generalization uses 50 episodes in each of three held-out kitchens without further adaptation. Recorded evaluation seeds The manuscript specifies stage seeds 50000–50049 for ACT and DP. GR00T uses 10001–10050, reused for each generalization scene and the long-horizon protocol. Record the seed manifest alongside each result. New comparison sweeps should use matched episode seeds across methods; do not imply the manuscript used identical seed ranges for every method. Scene-level uncertainty Generalization reports mean ± standard deviation across three scenes. The average row aggregates stage performance within each scene before reporting variation across scenes. The same frozen policy and episode-seed range are reused across native scenes within the corresponding evaluation run. Transitions without resets PPO, RLPD, ACT, DP and π0.5 switch between learned stage policies when the stage succeeds. GR00T uses one task model trained on pooled stage data, with a new instruction at each transition. Do not reset simulator state between stages of a complete sequence. title: Leaderboard protocol — DexArena
text: Leaderboard Score protocol Three evaluation tracks, explicit aggregation and a reproducible evidence trail. Manuscript baselines, not a verified community leaderboard The current scores are the six paper baselines. Public submission intake, remote execution and independent verification are not yet available. Evaluation units 01 Stage execution 30 stages × 50 episodes in the training scene. Each stage starts from its own valid reset distribution. 02 Cross-scene 30 stages × 3 native scenes × 50 episodes. Freeze the policy; retain the background manifest for every run. 03 Long-horizon 10 sequences × 50 episodes. Reset once per episode, never between stages; measure final sequence completion. How scores are aggregated Stage and long-horizon averages weight tasks equally. For cross-scene results, average stage success within each scene first, then report the mean and standard deviation across the three scene averages. The ± value is scene variation, not a training-seed confidence interval. The original manuscript records ACT/DP stage seeds 50000–50049 and GR00T seeds 10001–10050. New comparison sweeps should use matched episode seeds across methods and record the manifest; do not imply the paper used identical seed ranges for every method. Keep task horizons and physical success predicates fixed. Persistent hold counters or latches are part of the task definition. π0.5 switches stage models for composition; GR00T uses a pooled task model with stage instructions. Reproduction package Identity Environment/task revision, robot UID, controller, horizon and seeds. Policy Checkpoint hash, adapter revision, training-data scope and observation preprocessing. Scenes Background IDs, camera profile and source/geometry manifests. Outcomes Per-episode success, steps, stage trace, logs, videos and aggregation script. Explore results ↗ Rollouts & evidence ↗
